title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 283 (Custody of company’s properties)

content.overview: Where a winding-up order has been made or a provisional liquidator appointed, the Company Liquidator or provisional liquidator shall, on the order of the Tribunal, forthwith take into custody or control all the property, effects and actionable claims to which the company is or appears to be entitled and take necessary steps to protect and preserve them.
content.glance: On Tribunal order the liquidator must take custody of company property, effects and actionable claims and protect them.
content.study: Section 283 obliges the Company Liquidator or provisional liquidator, once directed by the Tribunal, to take immediate custody or control of all property, effects and actionable claims belonging or appearing to belong to the company and to protect and preserve them. This is the foundational control step after the winding-up order.

sections.heading: Custody
sections.body: On Tribunal order the liquidator takes into custody or control all property, effects and actionable claims of the company.

sections.heading: Protection
sections.body: The liquidator must take such steps and measures as may be necessary to protect and preserve the properties.

examples.title: Immediate custody
examples.body: After the winding-up order the Tribunal directs the liquidator to take custody; the liquidator must act forthwith and secure the assets.

hypotheticals.question: Who takes custody of company property after a winding-up order?
hypotheticals.analysis: The Company Liquidator or provisional liquidator, on the order of the Tribunal, under section 283.

misconceptions.trap: Directors retain custody until the liquidator chooses to take over.
misconceptions.correction: Section 283 requires the liquidator, on Tribunal order, to take custody forthwith.
